headline: HubSpot, the Cambridge, Massachusetts software company, is laying off about 660 workers, around 7% of its staff, as it shifts its strategy toward AI.
score_reason: Confirmed by the CEO's letter and reported by several outlets.
importance_line: About 660 people lose their jobs and the company is cutting management layers, but the CEO says the cuts are not driven by AI efficiencies, so how much AI is behind them rests on the company's own account.
summary: CBS News Boston reports that CEO Yamini Rangan told staff in a letter that HubSpot has shifted from building software that helps customers grow to delivering outcomes for them with AI, and that the company will have fewer management layers. Rangan wrote that the layoff decision 'is not driven by AI-related efficiencies', although the shift to AI is changing product, pricing and service; laid-off staff get 20 weeks of base pay plus a week per year of service, up to 30 weeks.
notes: CTech page returned no text; read CBS News Boston instead, which quotes the CEO's letter. Other outlets (Boston Globe, Fast Company, Quartz) carry it.
